correctness.rationale: For an ordered ell-tuple U of vertices with indegree zero, the probability no random image lands in U is ((n-ell)/n)^n, and conditional on this event the restriction to [n]\U is a uniform map whose entire cycle-length vector is unchanged. Summation over tuples proves the all-r factorial-pruning identity. The j-cycle expectation is b_{m,j}/j by prescribing j edges, yielding the exact covariance formula and j=1 zero, j>=2 strict negative signs. Expanding log b_{n,j} with j/sqrt(n)->x gives the Gaussian factor e^(-x²/2); expansion of b_{n-1,j}/b_{n,j} yields the -x e^(-x²/2)/(2e) scaled covariance. Exponential product bounds dominate summations, giving -1/(2e) for components and -sqrt(pi/8)/e for cyclic vertices after sqrt n scaling. Independently exhaustive small maps n=2..5 reproduce all cycle-length covariances and signs.
residual_risks: Mesoscopic limit assumes x>0 fixed; no claim of whole joint process limit or statistical independence for fixed point count.
